ns2:section.sectionText: SP25 - ENGL 396 - English Honors Seminar - The More-than-Human Middle Ages - Robert Barrett - The pages of medieval British and Irish literature abound with human and more-than-human agents: berserker warriors, asexual elephants, sympathetic werewolves, women made from flowers, apocalyptic floods, and more. In this course, we will explore the enmeshment of these diverse entities, paying particular attention to their deconstruction of the longstanding Eurowestern opposition between nature and culture. Our texts (which we will read in Modern English translation) include (but are not limited to) the debate poem The Owl and the Nightingale (in which the titular birds trade insults and strive for superiority), the Arthurian romance Sir Gawain and the Green Knight (in which Sir Gawain finds himself the object of an all-too-deadly hunt), the Fables of Scottish poet Robert Henryson (which use Aesop’s animals to meditate on the relationship between body and soul), and the Welsh Mabinogi (in which crafty wizards treat species difference, not as a barrier, but as a revolving door). Assignments will range from short papers aimed at inculcating research skills to a long essay putting those skills to use.
